The recovery improvement remains necessary on current main; the related merged cooldown work does not supersede it. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `b1d2cdcd5cd59d3e272067381275823d4b47aca4` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent recovery repair with meaningful regression coverage; the prior actionable finding is resolved. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The repository state identifies a MEMBER author, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply. Inspected recovery fixtures use real SQLite with fake providers; the adapter test uses real loopback HTTP, without claiming external quota or billing coverage. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The repository state identifies a MEMBER author, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply. Inspected recovery fixtures use real SQLite with fake providers; the adapter test uses real loopback HTTP, without claiming external quota or billing coverage. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Prior finding addressed: The GitHub commit diff adds canonical-cache pruning after successful publication. The corresponding regression starts with three retained rows and a cap of one, requires zero embedding requests, and checks the surviving cache and published content. The adjacent failed-rebuild control still requires cache preservation.
Current main still needs the recovery change: At the fetched main revision, full rebuilds still seed the shadow embedding cache and prune it before publication; publication still deletes and replaces the live cache from the shadow. Completed work therefore remains coupled to successful shadow publication.
Latest release comparison: The supplied latest release revision also contains shadow-cache seeding and pre-publication pruning. This check does not establish the proposed recovery behavior as shipped. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Memory Core converts workspace files and session transcripts into searchable text and vector indexes. Its embedding cache avoids repeated provider requests, while shadow databases keep incomplete rebuilds from replacing the published index. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Memory files and sessions] --> B[Prepare content chunks] B --> C{Cached embedding available?} C -->|Yes| E[Build shadow index] C -->|No| D[Embedding provider] D --> F[Validate and retain completed embeddings] F --> E E -->|Successful rebuild| G[Publish searchable index] H[Forget selected sessions] -->|Clear retained embeddings| F ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test growth** | Production net +251 lines; tests net +334 lines | Production growth implements durable cache writes and validation fences; test growth covers recovery, capacity, deletion, and publication failures. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-cache.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-base.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts`, and 8 more. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep one bounded, durable embedding cache independent of atomic index publication, with source validation and Forget invalidation preserving the documented deletion contract. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: complete embeddings during a full rebuild, fail before shadow publication, restart, and retry. Current main discards that shadow work; the supplied regressions exercise this order, but were not run in this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Separating reusable provider results from atomic index publication fixes the owning lifecycle without another cache or schema, and the follow-up restores successful-rebuild retention enforcement.
